I KNOW! I was looking through the stuff on DeviantArt, just going about my day, and then I'm like "hmm, we haven't had any King Arthur stories recently. What if King Arthur lived in a 70s themed futuristic compound?"

"Quickly m'lord, the starfolk depart ere long!" Sir Arthur urged his king's carriage onto the bridge that led to the tower of ash. Sat atop a rocky headlands, even from this distance one could make out the only entrance, a narrow slit cut vertically into its perfectly sealed sides and set higher than the tallest castle in the realm. It was accessible only via a narrow drawbridge at the end of the path.

Huge caravans of treasures followed in their wake, gifts to pile upon their otherworldly overlords. Though their tastes were obscure, no one, not even the bravest of knights dared question them. Lithium Salts extracted from hot springs, the crystallized remains of concentrated vinegar and entire barrels of clear spirits accompanied the odd assortment of unique plants and animals and of course as much gold as the treasury could spare.

Such was the price of a kingdom.

"Enter, humans!" a deep voice commanded.

The great white doors rose silently into a recess in the ceiling, revealing the cavernous entry halls lined on all sides and on many levels by skyfolk soldiers. Although their stinger weapons hung casually at their belts, even the lowliest servant in the king's caravan had heard of their evaporative powers.

An emissary approached. "Have you brought what we need?" it asked in a low, silky tone.

The king nodded.

It examined the offerings closely, taking its time to look at each item the servants laid out and tapping the surface of the glimmering tablet it held in its smooth, fingerless appendages. "Is that all?"

The king nodded. "Yes, I believe this will satisfy our masters."

The emissary left through a slit in the wall that appeared as he approached and vanished after his passage.

Deliberation began and the minutes passed. No one dared breathe.

Finally, the voice spoke once more, its raw power reverberating within the hall.

"Humans! Your gold, your chemicals, these we can use, but you have not brought us what we have asked! Again, you have failed!"

The king bent to his knee, and Sir Arthur immediately urged the rest of the party to do likewise before bending to his own.

"Your greatness!" the king appealed. "We have scoured the lands for the artifact. You told us to look within, and we have looked within. We have searched aboveground and below, in oceans and in deserts! If you would beseech more time, perhaps some more of your wisdom, we can find and recover this 'Grail' of yours!"

The floor began to rumble, and the people exchanged nervous glances. Low at first, the thrumming and vibrations rose in pitch and intensity. The room shook as the voice laughed at the ignorance of the pathetic beings that stood before it.

"You fools! The grail is not a 'thing'! You, a 'King', dare claim ownership over man, woman and child. You tax the sweat of their brow to fill your wagons. You think me a crying child to be appeased with pathetic gifts! You have failed the test!"

A sparkling glimmer shot out from a point near the ceiling, vapourising the king into a pile of ash.

"Now, Sir Arthur, rise as king! Leave, and do not return until you have found the Grail!"

I hate mosquitoes. I'm hypersensitive to them--I get big welts (at least the size of a nickle, up to the size of a quarter) from most mosquito bites.

So, I've learned what I can to do to avoid them. I'm not wild about deet--it helps, but doesn't always work. I also wouldn't want to put it on my dog because it's a neurotoxin, and dogs lick their fur.

Some herbs work, especially if you let them smolder on the fire's coals (and smoke itself is pretty good). Mosquitoes hate the sun--if you spend as much time as possible in the sun (even if covered head to toe in clothes to avoid sunburn) or in your sealed tent, you should be ok. Yeah, it's hot--but it beats mosquito bites.

Finally, for your dog, there's Buck Mountain Parasite Dust that works wonders. Put it on your pup before you get back into the car to go home, and again before you go in the house. It's yarrow, diatomaceous earth and neem. It's AMAZINGLY effective.

It's not a repellent, but you could maybe put some on your pup before you get out of the car, and treat your pup every night and every morning while you're camping--it should do the job pretty well. I don't know if that'd be enough to prevent lyme disease carrying ticks from infecting your pup, but it will kill the buggers before you get home. There is a vaccine for lyme disease, so definitely get that for your pup if you haven't. :)

Deet. Deet. Deet. It is all about percentage of deet. Limonene, Lemon whatever, Tea tree oils, special collars and any sort of natural remedy does not work. You can be a granola wholefoody, smell like deet and still be cool with the hipsters at starbucks. I apparently have the body type that brings all the flying ladies to the yard. (mosquitos that bite are females looking for a bloodmeal to produce a nice raft of eggs to lay in some still watter) If your camping trip is in a place with greater temperature fluctuations (colder is better), and less stagnant water (rivers with greater slope profiles are better) are key features to pick out in locations to go. A mosquito will not venture kilometers far from a place that is good for eggs. Also, the obvious morning and evening thing. I heard somewhere that clothing color plays a part, but I haven't personally noticed any difference between colors. Going on slow walks through vegitation can be problematic since mosquitos can wake up from their disturbed perch and score a meal. Playing fetch in tall grass and leaves near a river is a recipe for lots of bites. When you are sitting tight for the evening, a good solid campfire works better for me than any citronella candle and lantern. If your dog gets bugs in her ears, ever consider having the dog wear a hat? I'm sure there is something that is both not overly warm and has a the side strings.

About Deet... It isn't magic mosquito perfume that turns you into an inert tree to them. One note on deet from a personal experience, a mosquito will still go to land on an arm sprayed with deet. Then upon landing, take off and land inches away from the previous spot. If that spot is clear of the chemical, the straw comes out. Don't just mist your dog's backside and expect results. Spray your hands till wet and give your dog's belly a good rub. Sprays tend to get the tips of the hair strands, but mosquitos don't land on fur. They go for the warmest spots without fur. Absolute best dog owner ever would spray some deet on some TP and wipe those ears, butt, and balls. But you dont have to be amazing, tell fido to roll over and spray that can like it's cheap. Even though it isn't. You probably spent more on gas to get there, so spend a little more on spray and get stuff that works, and use an amount that works.
